```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(jnanalytics)
```

jnanalytics describes the journal market in transformative agreements as one
set of tidy tables. Reference tables describe journals and agreements once;
article tables hold the facts; aggregates are built from them for the
dashboard and quick analyses. All tables are built in Google BigQuery, in
`subugoe-collaborative.jn_analytics`, from Crossref (`cr_instant`) and OpenAlex
(`openalex_walden`), using the journal and institution lists of the
cOAlition S Journal Checker Tool (JCT) and the ESAC registry.
The reference tables and aggregates are also exported as Parquet files, kept
in the `parquet/` folder of the package repository with one version per
release; the column descriptions are stored in the Parquet metadata.

## Tables

```{r}
tables <- tibble::tribble(
  ~table, ~grain, ~where,
  "journals", "one row per journal in a transformative agreement", "package, Parquet, BigQuery",
  "journal_issns", "one row per ISSN", "package, Parquet, BigQuery",
  "agreements", "one row per transformative agreement", "package, Parquet, BigQuery",
  "agreement_journals", "one row per agreement and journal", "package, Parquet, BigQuery",
  "agreement_institutions", "one row per agreement and participating institution", "package, Parquet, BigQuery",
  "portfolios", "one row per dashboard page and agreement (ESAC ID); journals via agreement_journals", "package, Parquet, BigQuery",
  "articles", "one row per work with a DOI", "BigQuery",
  "article_first_authors", "one row per work, first-author institution and country", "BigQuery",
  "article_agreements", "one row per work, agreement, author role and institution match", "BigQuery",
  "journal_year", "works per journal, year and work type", "Parquet, BigQuery",
  "journal_year_country", "as journal_year, per first-author country", "Parquet, BigQuery",
  "journal_year_license", "works per journal, year, work type and CC licence", "Parquet, BigQuery",
  "journal_year_country_license", "works per journal, year, work type, first-author country and CC licence", "Parquet, BigQuery",
  "agreement_journal_year", "works covered per agreement, journal, year, work type and author role", "Parquet, BigQuery",
  "release", "one row describing the release", "Parquet, BigQuery"
)
stopifnot(setequal(tables$table, jn_tables()))
knitr::kable(
  dplyr::mutate(tables, table = paste0("[`", table, "`](#", gsub("_", "-", table), ")")),
  col.names = c("Table", "Grain", "Available in")
)
```

## Counting rules

- **Works.** All works with a DOI whose primary location is a journal in
  `journals`, published from 2016, of any OpenAlex type. Nothing is excluded
  in SQL. Filter on `work_type`; research articles are `article` and
  `review`.
- **Publication year.** OpenAlex `publication_year`. The Crossref year is
  kept in `articles.pub_year_crossref` for comparison; Crossref is matched by
  DOI only, never by date.
- **Open access.** Every work in a fully OA journal-year is OA. In a hybrid
  journal-year, a work is OA if Crossref has a Creative Commons licence for
  its version of record, whatever its start date, as in hoaddata 0.3 (CC
  BY-NC-SA in four delayed-OA journals does not count). `articles_oa` counts
  both. `articles_with_cc_license` counts the Crossref licence evidence
  alone; in fully OA journals it is a metadata indicator, not OA evidence.
  `articles_oa_openalex` counts works OpenAlex considers open at the
  publisher (`diamond`, `gold` or `hybrid`).
- **Hybrid or fully OA.** `journals.oa_model` is the current status from
  OpenAlex (`is_oa` or DOAJ) or the curated list. The aggregates carry an
  `oa_model` per year: a journal counts as hybrid up to and including its
  OpenAlex `oa_flip_year`, a transition year, and as fully OA afterwards.
  Publishers that turned all their journals fully OA at once are listed in
  `data-raw/manual/oa_flips.csv` (for example ACM from 2026); their hybrid
  journals count as hybrid up to the year before and fully OA from then on.
- **Countries.** First-author countries from OpenAlex, with full counting: a
  work with first-author affiliations in two countries counts in both. Take
  journal totals from `journal_year`, never by summing over countries.
- **Agreements.** A work is covered by an agreement if its journal is in the
  agreement, its OpenAlex publication date lies within the agreement period,
  and its first author's OpenAlex institution is a participating institution,
  one of its children or its parent (`direct`, `child`, `parent`). `related`
  institutions are kept in `article_agreements` but not counted. Agreements
  missing from ESAC get an inferred period (`agreements.is_period_inferred`).
- **Journals of an agreement.** Journal-level statistics per agreement
  (`jn_oa(by = "agreement_id")`) count all works in the journals an
  agreement covers, by default only in the years it ran. A journal in
  several agreements counts in each, so never sum over agreements. This is
  different from the works covered through authors' institutions above.
- **Additivity.** Every count in an aggregate can be summed over journals,
  years and work types. Shares are not stored; compute them, for example
  `articles_oa / articles` or, for Crossref metadata,
  `articles_with_orcid / articles_in_crossref`.

## Columns

```{r, results = "asis"}
for (table in tables$table) {
  schema <- jn_schema(table)
  cat("\n### ", table, " {#", gsub("_", "-", table), "}\n\n", sep = "")
  cat(tables$grain[tables$table == table], ". Available in: ",
      tables$where[tables$table == table], ".\n\n", sep = "")
  out <- data.frame(
    Column = paste0("`", schema$column, "`"),
    Type = paste0(schema$type, ifelse(schema$key, ", key", "")),
    Description = schema$description
  )
  print(knitr::kable(out))
  cat("\n")
}
```
